prerequisites: Prior knowledge necessary for the correct follow-up of the course, assessed by a preliminary test.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand and fluently manage concepts such as: linearity, dependence and independence, linear applications, matrices, determinants, systems of equations, changes of bases and systems, diagonalization, scalar product, quadratic forms, applications in affine Euclidean geometry.
Understand and manage the classical concepts, properties, and results of derivatives of real functions of one variable.
Understand and fluently manage concepts such as: indefinite integral, definite integral, approximate integration, improper integral.
Apply theoretical knowledge to the posing and solving of problems, mainly everyday and engineering-related, emphasizing scientific rigor and appropriate language use.
Recognize the above concepts in other fields and disciplines of engineering.
Develop analytical skills and rigorous logical thinking through the study of differential and integral calculus.

syllabus_topics: The field of complex numbers: definition, associated concepts, and forms of expression
Basic functions of complex variable: n-th root, exponential, logarithm, complex power, trigonometric functions
Problem seminar: Operations with complex numbers
Topic 4: Conics and quadrics. Quadratic forms (complementary)
Part 2: Differential and Integral Calculus in One Variable
Topic 5: Limits and continuity of functions of a real variable
Approximation of a function by Taylor polynomials
Topic 7: Integral calculus in one variable and applications
Integration by parts, substitution, simple fractions
Problem seminar: Calculation of primitives and applications

assessment_methods.method: Resolution and submission of theoretical-practical complementary activities

assessment_rules: A preliminary test ('Prueba 0') on prior knowledge must be passed with at least 7 out of 10 points for other assessments to be considered; otherwise, the final exam score is 0. The final exam (80% of the final grade) consists of two parts, each contributing 50% to the exam score. For the final exam score to be calculated normally, both parts must have a minimum score of 3; otherwise, the final exam score will be the minimum of 3 and the calculated score. Two non-recoverable complementary theoretical-practical activities (20% of the final grade) are also assessed. The final grade (NF) is calculated as: NF = (Final Exam Score * 0.8) + (Complementary Activities Score * 0.2). Students may use scores from continuous assessment activities to replace corresponding parts of the final exam if they scored 5 or more; otherwise, they must take the full final exam. If a part of the final exam is passed in the ordinary call, it carries over to the extraordinary call. The course is passed with a final grade of 5 or higher.
